How to get a GitHub token
Code Fix Panda needs a free GitHub personal access token to search for issues. It only reads public information, so your token needs no permissions at all.
Sign in at github.com. You can create a free account if you don\'t have one.
Open Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens → Tokens (classic), then choose Generate new token (classic). The button below takes you straight there.
Name it \"Code Fix Panda\" and pick an expiration. Leave every permission (scope) unchecked.
Tap Generate token, then copy the token. GitHub shows it only once, so copy it before leaving the page.
Come back here, paste it into the token box, and tap Save.
Your token stays on this device and is sent only to GitHub. A token saved here replaces any token built into the app.
Using the token built into this app. Enter your own below to replace it.
No token yet — the app can\'t search GitHub until you add one.
Looking to make a contribution on GitHub?
Select the kind of issues you would like to see
This list is built directly from matching issues, not from a separate repo search — every repo shown is guaranteed to have at least one open issue for whichever mode you\'re in.

The number on each card is simply how many matching issues that repo had in this batch — repos with more matches sort higher. It isn\'t a measure of the repo\'s overall popularity or health (stars, forks, how recently it was updated) the way an earlier version of this screen used — that data isn\'t available without extra lookups this version deliberately doesn\'t make yet.
A future update may add that context back for repos worth a closer look, without giving up the guarantee that every repo shown here actually has something open for you.
Removes every cached repo/issue list so the next load fetches live data. Bookmarks and hidden issues are kept.
GitHub isn\'t accepting the token this app is using (it may be expired, revoked, or otherwise invalid). Enter a new personal access token in Settings.
This app needs a GitHub personal access token to make live requests against the Search API. Enter one in Settings.
No rate limit data available yet.
This reflects GitHub\'s Search API limit specifically, which is separate from and stricter than the general REST API limit.

The limit renews every minute, and these numbers come from your most recent search, so they may already have reset. Opening a list that is saved on your device uses no searches. Load More, a language you have not opened yet, Check for New Repos and Refresh this repo each use one.

All matching issues in this repo are hidden.
Uses one API call against your rate limit.
Nothing hidden yet — tap the ✕ on any issue in a repo\'s list to remove it from view. It stays reversible: come back here to unhide it any time.
They\'ll reappear wherever they\'re still cached — Top Repos and repo lists alike.
No bookmarks yet — tap the ★ on any issue to save it here.
Maintainers choose these labels themselves; GitHub does not check them, so difficulty and quality vary from project to project.

Issues the project\'s maintainers marked as a good place for newcomers to start — usually small, clearly explained, and not needing deep knowledge of the code. A good fit if you are new to contributing. (GitHub\'s label for these is \"good first issue.\")
Issues where the maintainers say they would welcome outside help. They can be simple or quite involved, so they are less aimed at beginners. (GitHub\'s label for these is \"help wanted.\")
To use this app you need to set your GitHub token. It is free, takes about a minute, and needs no permissions.
The Get a token button on the welcome screen opens this page, with the token\'s name already filled in. Choose an expiration, then scroll down.
GitHub\'s new token form, with the name Code Fix Panda filled in
Pinch to zoom, drag to move, double-tap to reset
The Get a token button on the welcome screen opens this page
No permissions needed.\nDo not tick any box.
The app only reads public information, so the token can do almost nothing. Check that every box is empty, then tap Generate token.
The bottom of the form: every permission box is unticked, with the Generate token button
GitHub shows the token only once, so copy it before you leave the page.
GitHub\'s token page, showing the new token and its copy button
Come back to the welcome screen, paste the token you copied into the box, and tap Save. It stays on this device and is sent only to GitHub.
